item.title: Clear skies, calm winds expected in Pensacola Wednesday evening
item.dc:creator: newsroom

item.content:encoded:
Pensacola is looking at pleasant conditions Wednesday evening, with mostly clear skies and scattered cumulus clouds offering good visibility across the area, according to Florida Gulf Signal.

Weather conditions are favorable for outdoor activities. Temperatures are holding at 84 degrees with moderate east winds at 13.6 knots. The falling tide is expected to reach a low of 0.6 feet around 7:18 p.m., with the previous high of 1.4 feet occurring at 10:20 a.m.

Those planning to head to the beach or waterfront should expect calm conditions throughout the evening.

Emerald Moving & Storage has extended its climate-controlled storage and moving services in the Pensacola area, according to reporting from RCN Worldwide Media Network.

The company's expansion reflects growing demand for temperature and humidity-regulated storage options in the local market, where Florida's hot and humid climate can pose challenges for items sensitive to moisture and heat.

Climate-controlled facilities help protect furniture, electronics, documents, and other belongings from potential damage caused by temperature fluctuations and humidity. The service extension comes as the moving and storage industry continues to serve Pensacola's residential and commercial relocation needs.

item.title: 25 years after Danielle Bell vanished, Escambia County family still seeking answers
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: A quarter-century has passed since 14-year-old Danielle Bell disappeared from Cantonment, but her family refuses to let her case fade into silence. The Escambia County teen's vanishing in 2001 remains unsolved, and relatives continue pressing for leads and public awareness in hopes of finally bringing closure to one of Northwest Florida's…
item.content:encoded:
A quarter-century has passed since 14-year-old Danielle Bell disappeared from Cantonment, but her family refuses to let her case fade into silence. The Escambia County teen's vanishing in 2001 remains unsolved, and relatives continue pressing for leads and public awareness in hopes of finally bringing closure to one of Northwest Florida's longest-running missing-person cases.

According to WKRG-TV 5, the Bell family has organized vigils and outreach efforts over the years to keep Danielle's memory alive and renew community attention on what happened to her. Despite the passage of time and investigative efforts, critical questions about her disappearance remain unanswered.

The case underscores the persistent pain experienced by families of missing persons and the challenges law enforcement faces when leads grow cold. Authorities and the community continue to encourage anyone with information about Danielle Bell's whereabouts or circumstances surrounding her disappearance to come forward.

item.title: Sen. Scott Leads Hearing on U.S. Drug Manufacturing as Trump Admin Boosts Domestic Pharma
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott held a Senate Special Committee on Aging hearing Wednesday to push for stronger domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing and reduce American dependence on foreign suppliers, particularly China and India. The Florida Republican's effort follows a Trump administration announcement this week committing to increased investment in…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott held a Senate Special Committee on Aging hearing Wednesday to push for stronger domestic pharmaceutical manufacturing and reduce American dependence on foreign suppliers, particularly China and India. The Florida Republican's effort follows a Trump administration announcement this week committing to increased investment in onshore drug production—a move Scott had previously requested.

Scott has made pharmaceutical supply chain security a priority, citing national security concerns over reliance on foreign-made generic drugs and ingredients. Earlier this year, Scott and Ranking Member Kirsten Gillibrand introduced the CLEAR LABELS Act, which would require country-of-origin labeling on prescription drugs. That bill advanced through the Senate Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions Committee in July.

Wednesday's hearing featured testimony from Kurt Orlofski, CEO of PAI Pharma in New Jersey; Christine Baeder, president of Apotex USA and LATAM in Weston, Florida; and Mihir Torsekar, a senior economist with the Coalition for a Prosperous America. Scott emphasized that federal agencies must now award manufacturing contracts to American companies to translate the administration's commitment into tangible domestic production capacity.

Details on specific dates, times, and admission prices for this year's Haunted Trail have not yet been announced. Residents interested in attending or volunteering for the event are encouraged to reach out to the Wilmer Volunteer Fire Department directly for more information.

item.title: Sen. Rick Scott's Surrogacy Bill Blocked Again by Senate Democrats
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: U.S. Senator Rick Scott attempted to pass his Stopping Adversarial Foreign Exploitation of Kids in Domestic Surrogacy (SAFE KIDS) Act on the Senate floor Tuesday night, but Senate Democrats blocked the legislation by unanimous consent, marking the second time this year the bill has failed to advance. Scott's bill targets what he describes as a…
item.content:encoded:
U.S. Senator Rick Scott attempted to pass his Stopping Adversarial Foreign Exploitation of Kids in Domestic Surrogacy (SAFE KIDS) Act on the Senate floor Tuesday night, but Senate Democrats blocked the legislation by unanimous consent, marking the second time this year the bill has failed to advance.

Scott's bill targets what he describes as a national security threat: the practice of citizens from hostile nations, particularly China, using American surrogates to obtain U.S. citizenship for their children. The Florida Republican pointed to recent reporting from major outlets including The Wall Street Journal, CBS News, and New York Magazine that have highlighted exploitation and trafficking concerns tied to international commercial surrogacy arrangements.

"American citizenship is not for sale, and our enemies cannot be allowed to buy it," Scott said during his floor remarks. He noted the issue originated from a case affecting one of his Florida constituents, which prompted him to raise the alarm in July. Since then, he said, similar stories have gained national attention, underscoring what he views as a gap in U.S. law.

The SAFE KIDS Act would invalidate commercial surrogacy agreements involving citizens of adversarial nations—China, Iran, Russia, and North Korea—and create a misdemeanor penalty for brokers who knowingly or recklessly facilitate such arrangements. Surrogates themselves would not face criminal charges under the proposal. Currently, no federal law directly addresses international commercial surrogacy practices.

item.title: Fire Prevention Week warns of lithium-ion battery dangers starting Oct. 4
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: As rechargeable batteries power everything from phones to e-bikes, fire safety officials are raising alarm about the risks they pose if charged improperly or used carelessly. The National Fire Protection Association is making lithium-ion battery safety the focus of Fire Prevention Week, October 4-10, under the theme "Charge into Fire Safety: Safe…
item.content:encoded:
As rechargeable batteries power everything from phones to e-bikes, fire safety officials are raising alarm about the risks they pose if charged improperly or used carelessly. The National Fire Protection Association is making lithium-ion battery safety the focus of Fire Prevention Week, October 4-10, under the theme "Charge into Fire Safety: Safe Charging Is a Superpower!"

Lithium-ion batteries store enormous amounts of energy in compact spaces, and when damaged or charged incorrectly, they can overheat, ignite, or explode. While the NFPA hasn't yet compiled a national database of home fires involving these batteries, fire departments across the country are reporting a rising number of lithium-ion incidents. The campaign aims to educate the public about safer habits before the problem worsens.

The safety message is straightforward: always use the charger that came with your device or one approved by the manufacturer. Charge on hard, flat surfaces like tables or desks—never on beds, couches, or under pillows, where soft materials trap heat and block airflow. If a device feels extremely hot, begins to swell, smokes, or smells unusual, stop using it immediately and unplug it. Larger items like e-bikes and scooters should charge outdoors and away from building exits, since those batteries pack more energy and can fuel faster-spreading fires if they fail.

Other key tips include unplugging devices once fully charged rather than leaving them plugged in indefinitely, and keeping devices in sight while charging on aircraft—never in overhead compartments. Fire Prevention Week, observed every October since the early 1900s, relies on local fire departments and community organizations to spread these messages in neighborhoods throughout North America. More resources are available at fpw.org.

item.title: FDOT Details U.S. 90 Resurfacing Plans for Santa Rosa County
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The Florida Department of Transportation is opening its virtual project update for a major resurfacing effort on U.S. 90 in Santa Rosa County, with details becoming available Thursday at noon. The project will resurface all existing travel lanes, auxiliary lanes, and paved shoulders along the corridor. FDOT also plans to add a left-turn lane for…
item.content:encoded:
The Florida Department of Transportation is opening its virtual project update for a major resurfacing effort on U.S. 90 in Santa Rosa County, with details becoming available Thursday at noon.

The project will resurface all existing travel lanes, auxiliary lanes, and paved shoulders along the corridor. FDOT also plans to add a left-turn lane for eastbound traffic and a right-turn lane for westbound traffic at Jeff Ates Road, plus upgrades to pedestrian features to meet Americans with Disabilities Act standards. The improvements won't require any additional right of way purchases.

Project maps, drawings, and other materials will be available on the U.S. 90 resurfacing project webpage starting Thursday. The public can also review information by contacting FDOT Project Manager Dean Mitchell at (850) 415-9016, via email at dmmitchell@hntb.com, or by mail at 1282 Office Park Drive, Chipley, FL 32428. Construction bids are scheduled for late 2027.

item.title: Florida Democrats to Outline Affordability Platform as Vote-by-Mail Ballots Arrive
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried will host a virtual press call Thursday morning with state legislative candidates to discuss the party's affordability agenda as vote-by-mail ballots begin reaching voters statewide. The briefing, scheduled for 10 a.m. on Zoom, will feature Senator Brian Nathan (Senate District 14), Representative Emily…
item.content:encoded:
Florida Democratic Party Chair Nikki Fried will host a virtual press call Thursday morning with state legislative candidates to discuss the party's affordability agenda as vote-by-mail ballots begin reaching voters statewide.

The briefing, scheduled for 10 a.m. on Zoom, will feature Senator Brian Nathan (Senate District 14), Representative Emily Gregory (House District 87), and three legislative candidates: Richard Lamondin (Senate District 38), Nik Dean (House District 38), and Lucia Baez-Geller (House District 106). Democrats say the forum will focus on lowering costs and raising wages while highlighting recent seat flips they attribute to voter focus on affordability issues.

The call comes as Florida heads into the final stretch of its 2026 campaign cycle. Democrats have emphasized that their candidates are concentrating messaging on pocketbook issues—housing costs, wages, and support for seniors—rather than what party officials describe as Republican efforts to distract from economic challenges. The party is attempting to break Republican supermajorities in the state legislature.

Journalists interested in attending the Zoom call must RSVP through the Florida Democratic Party's registration link.

item.title: Sen. Moody Pushes Federal Women's Sports Protection Bill at Senate Hearing
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Senator Ashley Moody joined female athletes at a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing Wednesday to advocate for federal legislation aimed at restricting transgender athletes from competing in women's sports programs. The hearing, titled "Standing Up for Women in Sports: Ensuring Opportunity, Fairness and Safety for Female Athletes," featured Moody's…
item.content:encoded:
Senator Ashley Moody joined female athletes at a Senate Judiciary Committee hearing Wednesday to advocate for federal legislation aimed at restricting transgender athletes from competing in women's sports programs. The hearing, titled "Standing Up for Women in Sports: Ensuring Opportunity, Fairness and Safety for Female Athletes," featured Moody's call for what she characterized as fairness and safety in women's athletics.

"Male athletes have no business competing in women's sports, and it's mindboggling that in 2026 we must pass legislation to protect meaningful opportunity for girls to compete," Moody said, according to her office. The Florida senator is a cosponsor of the Protection of Women and Girls in Sports Act of 2025, which would generally prohibit school athletic programs from allowing individuals assigned male at birth to participate in women's and girls' programs.

Moody's push at the federal level builds on her previous work in Florida. As the state's attorney general, she led a multistate legal challenge to the Biden administration's 2024 Title IX regulation changes, arguing they undermined protections for women and girls. Florida itself enacted the Fairness in Women's Sports Act in 2021, which restricts individuals assigned male at birth from participating in sports teams designated for women or girls.

Moody is also a cosponsor of the Title IX Clarification Act of 2026, which would define sex under Title IX as biological sex and clarify that gender identity does not change that classification. The legislation reflects an ongoing national debate over transgender athlete participation in school sports.

item.title: Last Marine Harrier jet arrives at Pensacola museum after final mission
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: The final AV-8B Harrier jet ever produced for the U.S. Marine Corps has completed its last flight and been delivered to the National Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola for permanent display. Bureau Number 166288 arrived at the museum after being demilitarized and made safe for static exhibition, marking the end of an era for the iconic…
item.content:encoded:
The final AV-8B Harrier jet ever produced for the U.S. Marine Corps has completed its last flight and been delivered to the National Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola for permanent display. Bureau Number 166288 arrived at the museum after being demilitarized and made safe for static exhibition, marking the end of an era for the iconic vertical-takeoff aircraft.

The jet, delivered by Boeing in September 2003, accumulated more than 5,800 flight hours during its operational service, including multiple combat deployments. The Harrier's unique ability to take off and land vertically made it a cornerstone of Marine air operations for decades, though the service has since transitioned to the newer F-35B Lightning II fighter.

The museum's acquisition of BuNo 166288 adds a significant piece to its collection of naval aviation history. The National Naval Aviation Museum, located at Naval Air Station Pensacola, preserves and displays aircraft and artifacts spanning more than a century of naval flight operations. The Harrier's arrival underscores the museum's role in honoring the aircraft and aviators that have shaped Marine and Navy aviation.

item.title: ECPS, Magdalene's Host Free Online Safety Workshop for Parents, Kids
item.dc:creator: newsroom
item.description: Escambia County Public Schools is teaming up with local anti-trafficking organization Magdalene's, Inc. to offer a free community education event on the dangers children face online, with two session dates scheduled for mid-October. The workshop, titled "Playing It Safe: Exposing Dangers in Our Digital World," will bring together school district…
item.content:encoded:
Escambia County Public Schools is teaming up with local anti-trafficking organization Magdalene's, Inc. to offer a free community education event on the dangers children face online, with two session dates scheduled for mid-October.

The workshop, titled "Playing It Safe: Exposing Dangers in Our Digital World," will bring together school district leaders, law enforcement, and Dr. Andrew Doan, an expert in media addiction, to discuss the risks young people encounter through smartphones, gaming, social media, and other internet activity. According to the district, over 500,000 online predators are active at any given time, making digital safety education critical for parents, guardians, educators, and community members.

The event is designed for ages 13 and up and will cover what children encounter online, current protections in place within ECPS, and practical steps families can take if they spot suspicious activity. "The No. 1 priority of Escambia County Public Schools is to protect our students," the district said in announcing the partnership.

Two identical sessions are scheduled for October 13 and October 15. Seating is limited, and registration is encouraged through Eventbrite. The event is free and open to all community members. More information and registration links are available through the school district.

A historic aircraft has completed its two-week journey from Pensacola to the Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum in Colorado, arriving Wednesday at its new home.

According to KKTV 11 News, the plane made the cross-country trek from Pensacola, marking a significant transfer for the historic aircraft. The Pueblo Weisbrod Aircraft Museum, located in Colorado, specializes in restoring and preserving vintage and historic aircraft.

Details about the specific aircraft type and its historical significance were not immediately available, but the long-distance delivery highlights the logistical challenges involved in moving historic aviation treasures across the country.

item.title: ECUA Pushes Deadline for 2026 Customer Survey
item.dc:creator: newsroom

The survey gives ECUA customers a chance to share feedback on service, billing, and other aspects of the utility's operations. Participation helps the authority…
item.content:encoded:
The Emerald Coast Utilities Authority is reminding customers they have until Thursday, September 30 to complete the 2026 Customer Survey, according to a release from the utility.

The survey gives ECUA customers a chance to share feedback on service, billing, and other aspects of the utility's operations. Participation helps the authority understand what's working well and where improvements may be needed.

Customers can find the survey through ECUA's website or may receive information about participating by mail. With just over a week left before the deadline, ECUA is encouraging anyone who hasn't yet filled out the brief questionnaire to do so before September 30.
